newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-FUSION IS NICKNAME FOR MLS MIAMI TEAM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FUSION IS NICKNAME FOR MLS MIAMI TEAM.

text.p: The new Major League Soccer franchise in Miami will be nicknamed the Fusion and play its home games in the Orange Bowl, the league and the team announced Tuesday.

Miami, which has a 10-year lease to play home games at the Orange Bowl, was selected along with Chicago as expansion cities earlier this season as the league will grow to 12 teams in 1998. The Chicago team remains unnamed.

Miami will be the second Florida city with an MLS franchise, joining the Tampa Bay Mutiny. Communications entrepreneur Ken Horowitz led an investment group that successfully bid $20 million for the franchise.

The MLS and the investment group believe the large Latin American community in the greater-Miami area will help the Miami Fusion find success. Horowitz said that the melting pot aspects of the city led to the selection of the nickname.
"The name Fusion symbolises the relationship between the world's most exciting sport and Miami's multicultural makeup," said Douglas Logan, MLS commissioner.
